text:
O Lord! God of hosts,

eternal Father, eternal King,

for this world you created

through the virtue of your power;

because you said: let there be light,

and at your word there was light;

because you coexist with the Word,

because with you the Word is

from age to age

and without tomorrow and without yesterday,


requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine,


et lux perpetua luceat eis!


O Jesus Christ, for the cold

of your Bethlehem manger,

for your anguish in the Garden,

for the vinegar and the gall,

for the thorns and the rods

with which I tore your flesh,

and for the cross on which you erased

all the sins of Israel;

Son of Man, desolate,

tragic God, terrible Judge:


requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine,


et lux perpetua luceat eis!


Divine Spirit, Paraclete,

breath of great Yahweh,

who joins Father to Son,

and being One, you are Three;

for the white-winged dove,

for the inviolate virginity

of that Virgin who in her womb

carried the Messiah Emmanuel;

for the burning red tongues

with which you inspired knowledge and faith

in the beloved disciples

of Jesus Christ, our good:


requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine,


et lux perpetua luceat eis!

translation.title: Requiem
translation.editorial_note: The Latin liturgical refrain is retained; the Spanish rendering’s “con que tus carnes desgarré” remains in the first-person voice supplied by the source.
